summary.text:
Thinner than North Norfolk, and honestly labelled as such. What we hold from the 23 February Council is Minute 488 itself — a two-page resolution referring the strategy through — and neither the TMSS in Appendix 1 nor the Capital Strategy in Appendix 2 that it approves. The only two numbers in the paper are the borrowing limits set for 2026/27: £25m overall, £16m short-term (Recommendation 1, p2).

Nothing else is testable. No CFR, no external borrowing, no MRP policy content, no prudential indicators, no maturity profile. The balance-sheet identity cannot be computed and no reconciliation is possible from this paper. On our own side, our PWLB file has no record for Stratford-on-Avon DC at all — searching 'Stratford-on-Avon', 'Stratford' and 'Avon' returns neighbouring authorities but nothing for the council. Taken with the paper's own phrasing that it sets Prudential Indicators 'whether or not it decided to borrow', the plain reading is that this is a nil-PWLB district and the £25m limit runs to headroom. That is offered to them as ours to be corrected on, not asserted about their position.

Contact is thin: only Democratic Services (committeemanagers@stratford-dc.gov.uk) is addressed on the paper, no named finance officer, no S151. A short honest email is drafted in the North Norfolk shape — acknowledging what we do not hold, offering our nil-PWLB position for correction, and giving inter-authority market context that a small district might find useful. It needs an officer address before sending; fetching Appendix 1 is the single highest-value next step here.

officer.body:
Hi [name],

Apologies for the cold email. PWLBtoday is fairly new so you may not have come across us yet.

We're built for local authority treasury teams and nothing else: live PWLB rates at both daily fixings, a monthly breakdown of every loan the sector draws, every council's PWLB book priced daily against the DMO's repayment curve, and a training academy for officers and members. There's more — the predictor, the SONIA path, peer metrics, a daily brief — in the brochure at [BROCHURE URL]. We don't sell treasury products, and the data side is free and stays free.

To keep that data and our training relevant we built tools that watch committee papers across every council in the country, so we can see how a council's own figures compare with where the market has gone since. Normally that means we write with something specific about a council's own numbers. This one is shorter and more honest than most: what we hold from your 23 February Council is Minute 488 itself, the two-page resolution, and not the TMSS in Appendix 1 or the Capital Strategy in Appendix 2 that it approves. So nothing below is a comment on your position, and we haven't guessed at one.

The one thing we can offer runs the other way, from our data to you. Our PWLB file has no record of any borrowing at all for Stratford-on-Avon District Council — searching under the council's name and under the neighbouring authorities returns nothing for you. Taken at face value that would mean no PWLB debt outstanding, which read together with the phrasing in your paper — that the Council sets Prudential Indicators 'whether or not it decided to borrow' — is consistent with a nil-PWLB position and your £25m overall borrowing limit running to headroom. We hold PWLB only, so any drawings from other authorities or the banks would sit outside our file entirely, and Appendix 1 will say what our data cannot. What we do hold for you is visible at pwlbtoday.org/loan-analysis.

For context on the market a low- or no-debt district might use on the placement side: Bank Rate is 3.75%, one-year PWLB certainty closed at 4.95% this afternoon on notice 314/26, and July's sector borrowing was £368m across 33 loans from just 19 borrowers at an average 5.02% — a thin market on the drawing side, which is itself informative if you're pricing deposits with other authorities on the placement side. The monthly breakdown is at pwlbtoday.org/pwlb-activity.

On training, three would probably fit best. Liability Benchmark: the essentials — the indicator gets more useful the smaller the debt book is, because it tells you precisely when internal borrowing stops being the cheaper option. Money Market Funds (CNAV / LVNAV / VNAV), for the investment side. And Audit Committee Chair (Treasury) for members. All 115 courses are free to local authorities until the end of September at pwlbtoday.org/academy, and free accounts for the whole team.

And if you do find it useful, mentioning it to others would help us more than anything. We're small, word of mouth is most of our marketing, and every sign-up helps us prove the need.

Sign up free → https://pwlbtoday.org/
Follow on LinkedIn → https://www.linkedin.com/company/pwlbtoday/
